heading: Joe’s Plan to Clean Up the Washington Swamp
text: 1 Congress Is Not a Stock Exchange Investigate Congressional Insider Trading When members of Congress make suspiciously well-timed trades, the American people deserve answers. Joe supports serious investigations into potential congressional insider trading and real accountability whenever a public official uses privileged information or public office for personal financial gain.

heading: Joe’s Plan to Clean Up the Washington Swamp
text: 2 Congress Is Not a Retirement Plan Enact Term Limits Joe supports firm congressional term limits so new leaders can rise, new ideas can be heard, and public officials remember that they work for the people. Experience has value, but Washington was never supposed to become a lifetime career.

heading: Joe’s Plan to Clean Up the Washington Swamp
text: 3 Congress: Put Away the Credit Card Balanced Budget Central Florida families cannot spend without limits, ignore the bill, and leave the balance to their children. Congress should not be allowed to do it either. Joe supports a balanced budget amendment requiring Washington to live within its means, confront wasteful spending, and make honest decisions about national priorities. The national debt clock should be a warning, not a scoreboard.

heading: A Life Built on Hard Work, Family, and Opportunity
text: Joe Strada is a Central Florida job creator and advocate for the skilled trades. He built a family-owned company from the ground up, helped create thousands of jobs, and invested in paid training so people could earn a living while learning a career.

heading: Hard Work from Day One
text: Joe Strada started working young. While still in high school he took a job as a handyman at a bowling alley to earn extra money, learning to fix what was broken and finish what he started. That habit - show up, solve the problem, take responsibility - became the foundation for everything that followed.

heading: Hard Work from Day One
text: He entered the trades because it was practical and honest work with a clear path forward for anyone willing to learn. It also taught him something that shaped his outlook for decades: skill and effort matter more than credentials.

heading: From One Van to a National Company
text: Joe grew Strada Services into a family-owned company that serves communities across the country. He learned to meet payroll, manage costs, keep customers satisfied, and navigate the regulations that shape every decision an employer makes.

heading: From One Van to a National Company
text: Along the way, Joe helped create thousands of jobs and established a company culture that promotes from within. Many of the company's leaders started in entry-level roles and worked their way up.

heading: Paid Training and Real Career Pathways
text: Joe has long believed a four-year degree should not be the only respected path to a good life. He invested in paid training programs so people could learn a trade, earn while they learned, and begin a career without taking on heavy debt.

heading: Paid Training and Real Career Pathways
text: That experience is why workforce development, apprenticeships, and career and technical education are central to his campaign. He has watched training change families' futures.

heading: Father, Grandfather, Neighbor
text: Joe and his wife raised their family in Central Florida, and much of his motivation for running is generational. He wants his children and grandchildren to inherit a country where hard work is rewarded, opportunity is real, and the next generation is not buried under debt.

heading: Father, Grandfather, Neighbor
text: Faith, family, and community service remain at the center of his life.

heading: A Common-Sense Outsider, Not a Career Politician
text: Joe is not seeking a career in politics. He is running because Congress needs more people who have signed the front of a paycheck, built something real, and lived with the consequences of policies written far from the job site.

heading: A Common-Sense Outsider, Not a Career Politician
text: He is running as a common-sense outsider focused on affordability, opportunity, accountability, and delivering practical results for the people of District 11.

heading: Job Creator
text: Joe has made payroll, balanced budgets, and fought through Washington's red tape for decades. He knows what it takes to keep the lights on and doors open.

heading: Workforce advocate

heading: Problem-solver
